votes.question: On Passage — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: This bill generally bars members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks, and it requires public notice before they sell. A Yea passes it in the House. A Nay votes against passage.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Stop Insider Trading Act (H R 7008)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: The Stop Insider Trading Act would bar members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks and would require public notice before a sale. This vote would have replaced that bill with a broader ban that also forces members, the President, the Vice President, and their spouses and dependent children to sell covered investments they already hold. A Yea would have made that swap; a Nay kept the original bill.

posts.text:
I’m proud to have supported the Kay Hagan Tick Reauthorization Act in the House, now signed into law. It reauthorizes up to $150 million over five years for Lyme and tick-borne disease research, prevention, and public health response.

This matters on Long Island, where Suffolk County reported more than 3,100 cases of Lyme disease in 2024 alone. Tick-borne illnesses are a serious local public health challenge that affects our families, kids, pets, and anyone who enjoys our parks, trails, and beaches.

As a member of the House Appropriations Committee, I’ll fight to fully fund these efforts and make sure Suffolk County gets its fair share for better research, prevention, detection, and treatment.

Seeing more dolphins make themselves at home off Long Island is an encouraging sign of the progress we’re making toward cleaner, healthier waters. I’m proud to have helped secure more than $120 million for the Long Island Sound since taking office and I’ll keep fighting to protect this treasured part of our environment and way of life.

This Breast Cancer Awareness Month, we honor survivors, remember the loved ones we’ve lost, and recognize how deeply a diagnosis changes a family’s life.

In Congress, I’ve supported $130 million for the Breast Cancer Research Program to advance breakthrough research, clinical trials, prevention, detection, and better treatments.

To those fighting breast cancer and the loved ones beside them, we stand with you.
From bringing home federal funding to cutting through red tape and returning millions to constituents, my team and I are delivering real results for Suffolk County every day. https://t.co/WVuKo0rGWO

I drew a line in the sand: I wouldn’t support my party’s tax bill without a meaningful fix to the $10,000 SALT cap I inherited. After a LOT of fighting, we quadrupled the SALT cap for five years and, combined with lower taxes on tips, overtime, and for seniors, are saving the average Long Island family about $3,000, now it’s Albany’s turn to address why New Yorkers are paying such high taxes in the first place.

Congratulations to Stony Brook University on being named New York’s No. 1 public university for the fifth consecutive year.

This recognition is a testament to the excellence of its students, faculty, and researchers and to the groundbreaking work happening across the university.

I’m proud to support that mission in Congress by securing critical federal funding to ensure Stony Brook can keep pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

roll_calls.question: On Motion to Recommit — Take Care of America’s Veterans Act (H R 9237)
roll_calls.plain_language: H.R. 9237 (Take Care of America’s Veterans Act) addresses veterans’ benefits, health care, counseling, Department of Veterans Affairs personnel, VA infrastructure, and the Veterans Community Care Program. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
